newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks crack historic 5,000 points.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks crack historic 5,000 points.

text.p: Mexican stocks surged above the 5,000-point barrier for the first time ever at the open on Thursday.
Bulls that flooded the market during the previous session kept charging on year-low U.S. long bond yields and a cheaper peso, dealers said.
The leading IPC share index was up 27.50 points in the opening 10 minutes, or 0.55 percent, at a record 5,001.73 points.

"It seemed unthinkable, but we're there, and what's even more incredible is there are floods of foreign investors and they're still buying -- not a profit-taker in sight," one excited floor trader said.

"Banco de Mexico upped its dollar put auction to $500 million, and that tells us they'll try to stop the peso getting too strong, so that makes our stocks a cheaper option for foreign investors," another desk trader said.
